summary.intent: Unlock TurboQuant KV cache compression on a Framework Desktop with Strix Halo iGPU (gfx1151) to enable 2× context extension with 30–77% KV memory savings, following a BIOS UMA change the user had just made.
summary.outcome: BIOS UMA change confirmed (VRAM 0.5 GB → 64 GB, not 108 GB target due to missing Auto option), email pipeline validated via Gmail MCP drafts, and a full audit revealed 0xSero/turboquant v0.2.0 is already installed with Triton kernels — but the critical PyTorch ROCm wheel ISA gap for gfx1151 remains unresolved and untested. No TurboQuant dispatch was achieved.

repo: 0xSero/turboquant v0.2.0 is installed as a Python egg in cohezion/.venv with Triton kernels (fused_rotate_quantize_kernel), vLLM attention backend plugin, and benchmarks — integration is via VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND, not a --kv-cache-dtype CLI flag
research/turboquant/ exists in the main worktree (not the dreamy-jingling-thacker worktree); stashed per MISSION_JOURNAL.md as Wave 4 deferred work
turboquant_axis dict is already injected into every inference payload; cache-gateway unlock sets TRITON_AMD_WMMA=1 + HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.1

Session 94 (2026-04-16) documented that PyTorch ROCm wheels lack valid ISA for gfx1151 — yields Invalid Device Function / Memory access fault on first Triton dispatch; this is a wheel issue, not a driver issue
Lemonade fleet lanes: NPU:13306 (only live lane), iGPU:13307/:13308, CPU:13309 — most lanes are placeholder daemons with no loaded model
vLLM 0.19.0 in cohezion/.venv is broken: torch 2.5.1+rocm6.2 lacks torch._inductor.custom_graph_pass that vLLM 0.19.0 requires; also has no TurboQuant support
local_environment_quirks.md is the canonical distillation of session-94 findings; TURBOQUANT_UNLOCK_REPORT.md referenced there no longer exists on disk

llama.cpp PR #20969 cited in the plan is a discussion thread, not a PR; real upstream TurboQuant PRs are #21089 (CPU-only, merged candidate) and community forks: TheTom (HIP/ROCm), paudley (Vulkan/RDNA 3.5)
Strix Halo memory model: model buffers land in GTT (shared system memory) not VRAM for UMA APUs; rocm-smi VRAM Used stays flat while GTT Used grows — this is expected behavior
EmailNotifier class is imported by 5+ scripts but has no class definition in tracked code — orphaned import pattern

code.finding: 0xSero/turboquant v0.2.0 — CUDA-tested Triton kernels, no AMD/gfx1151/HIP markers; Triton may auto-select backend but wheel-ISA bug may cause dispatch failure on gfx1151
Returns silently when GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD is missing — silent-failure anti-pattern; new send_handoff.py raises SystemExit(2) instead

New consolidated email script (90 lines): MIMEMultipart alternative with text/plain + text/html, raises EmailNotConfigured with remediation text on missing credential, lazy import of optional markdown2
Known-good llama.cpp launcher using Lemonade orchestrator with tested flags: -fa 1 -ngl 99, HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.1
PyTorch oracle (178 lines) for correctness gating — separate from 0xSero kernels; used to verify dispatch output matches paper tolerances
Canonical record of session-94 findings: PyTorch ROCm wheel ISA gap for gfx1151, AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 workaround, NPU/FLM path as recommended TurboQuant unlock

workflow: Gmail MCP create_draft bypasses SMTP credential management entirely — drafts land in Gmail for human review/send; cleaner than smtplib for interactive sessions where no credential is configured
llama.cpp default -fit on hangs at 99% CPU for minutes on large GGUF models on this host; always pass -fit off explicitly
Kernel version in a plan document does not mean it exists; Ubuntu mainline lacked 6.18.4 (build failed) — 6.18.23 is the actual latest longterm build
For APU/UMA systems, rocm-smi reports full allocated VRAM but HSA per-process ceiling may show ~half; GTT exposes 128 GB for spillover — not a bug
Prior session handoff artifacts (SESSION_HANDOFF_*.md, CONTINUE.md, GEMINI.md) should be read before planning any work to avoid duplicating already-completed phases
Adding a third-party apt PPA is a persistent system change (future apt updates pull from it indefinitely) — warrants explicit consent separate from the kernel upgrade itself
11 near-identical send_*.py scripts in /scripts indicate sprint-by-sprint proliferation rather than consolidation; a single parameterized script is the correct abstraction

open_items: Run smoke test: import turboquant.triton_kernels.fused_rotate_quantize_kernel, feed 2048×128 FP16 K tensor on iGPU, verify Triton JIT compiles for gfx1151 and dispatch completes without Invalid Device Function
Resolve PyTorch ROCm wheel ISA gap for gfx1151 — determine if newer torch wheel ships gfx1151 ISA or if NPU/FLM path is the only viable TurboQuant dispatch path
Evaluate paudley's Vulkan/RDNA 3.5 llama.cpp fork as fallback if Triton dispatch fails — Vulkan is driver-agnostic and architecturally matches gfx1151
BIOS firmware update to v3.05+ to expose UMA Auto, AI Max Performance, and PCIe Gen5 options — would potentially unlock VRAM beyond 64 GB via dynamic UMA scaling
Kernel 6.17 → 6.18.23 upgrade — deferred pending evidence it's needed; only confirmed necessary if Triton smoke test fails with wheel-ISA error that a newer torch/kernel would fix
ROCm 7.2.1 → 7.2.2 upgrade via amdgpu-install --rocmrelease=7.2.2 — deferred; clean path exists but reboot required
Consolidate 11 near-identical send_*.py scripts into the new send_handoff.py; delete redundant scripts
Fix EmailNotifier orphaned import — class definition missing from tracked code; 5+ scripts import it
